liveRoast.title: Title *
liveRoast.noSerialPortsDetected: No serial ports detected -- plug your adapter in, then ↻.
liveRoast.separateDrivePortPlaceholder: only if your own wiring needs a 2nd connection for Air/Drum
liveRoast.usingProfileHint: Using the "{{name}}" register map -- the advanced fields below don't apply while a profile is selected. Pick "Custom" above to go back to setting individual registers by hand.
liveRoast.advancedModbusHint: Leave any of these blank to use the FZ-94 defaults above. Only worth touching once you've confirmed your own unit's actual register map differs (see the VFD's own nameplate/front-panel parameters, or a real probe's slave ID). BT/ET/DT/Burner are confirmed against a shipped FZ-94 machine preset and its interpreting source code — exposed here for a genuinely different Modbus roaster, not because a real FZ-94 should need them changed. Air/Drum (control+feedback registers, operating range) and the Burner SV°C range are that engine's least-confirmed, blog-sourced defaults.
liveRoast.burnerSvPairHint: Air/Drum min+max and the Burner SV min+max only take effect as pairs — set both sides or neither.
liveRoast.ms6514Hint: Direct USB read of the Mastech MS6514 — reads straight over USB, no other software needed. Read-only. T1 → BT, T2 → ET. Keep the meter's display set to "T1" or "T2" (not "T1-T2") for reliable dual-channel reading. Every milestone (Charge, Dry End, FC Start, Drop, etc.) is a manual click — mark them yourself as the roast happens.
liveRoast.aillioHint: Talks directly to the roaster over USB (no port/host to configure — the app finds it by its own USB vendor/product id). Heater/Fan/Drum read back the device's own last-reported state, same "don't clobber real state" behavior as Direct Modbus.
liveRoast.tc4Hint: Direct USB read/write of a TC4+ shield running the aArtisanQ (PID) firmware, 115200 baud — talks straight over USB, no other software needed. Channel 1 → BT, channel 2 → ET, channel 3 (if wired) → DT. Heater and Fan sliders send real OT1/DCFAN commands; there's no Drum output on TC4, so that slider doesn't do anything here.
liveRoast.autoDetectMilestones: Auto-detect Charge/Dry End/FC Start from BT (opt-in)
liveRoast.dryEndThreshold: Dry End BT threshold (°C, blank to disable)
liveRoast.fcStartThreshold: FC Start BT threshold (°C, blank to disable)
liveRoast.startingControlsHintAlways: Sent as the roast's first command right after START, and used as the Controls panel's starting position.
liveRoast.startingControlsHintPresetOnly: Only applied at START when loaded from a saved preset (see "Load saved config" above) -- a fresh start like this one leaves the roaster wherever it already is, so it's not clobbered by an unrelated stale value. Otherwise these are just what gets saved into a new preset below.
liveRoast.milestonesHintPreset: Burner/Air/Drum start from this preset's saved values (see the Device tab), sent right after START -- from then on, the Controls panel on the Live Roast page reads and shows whatever the roaster is actually doing.
liveRoast.milestonesHintNoPreset: Burner/Air/Drum aren't set here -- once connected, the Controls panel on the Live Roast page reads and shows whatever the roaster is actually doing (from the device itself, not a guess), and nothing is written to it until you move a slider yourself.
liveRoast.pressOnHint: Press ON above when you're ready to connect.
liveRoast.mastechHint: Reading {{port}} directly — no other software needed. Read-only, this meter has no command to control anything. Every milestone (Charge, Dry End, FC Start, Drop, etc.) is a manual click — mark them yourself below.
liveRoast.resizeChartHandle: Drag to resize the chart row (controls/chart/Small Readout follow it)
liveRoast.modbusLiveHint: The controls beside the chart read and write directly over {{target}}: Burner is a drum-temperature setpoint (register 5, default 100–250°C — not a power %, shown as both a % slider and a direct °C slider that move each other), Air and Drum are VFD drives (run/stop + frequency registers 8192/8193, default 0–100%/0–70%), each with its own feedback register (8451) reporting the drive's actual current speed. Out-of-range values are clamped to the configured range. See "Advanced Modbus register map" above to override any of these for your own unit. Every milestone (Charge, Dry End, FC Start, Drop, etc.) is a manual click — mark them yourself as the roast happens.
liveRoast.tc4LiveHint: Reading/writing {{port}} directly (115200 baud, aArtisanQ/PID firmware) — no other software needed. The Heater/Fan sliders beside the chart send real OT1/DCFAN commands; there's no Drum output on TC4, so that slider doesn't do anything here. Heater/Fan readouts stay blank — TC4's own READ command only reports temperature channels, not its current output duty. Every milestone (Charge, Dry End, FC Start, Drop, etc.) is a manual click — mark them yourself as the roast happens.

autoControlPanel.heading: Automatic control
autoControlPanel.intro: Starts at Charge. Moving any slider by hand takes over from it. Check the roaster is behaving before leaving it to run, and keep your hand near the Emergency stop.
autoControlPanel.safetyDisabled: Roaster safety is disabled in Settings -- Emergency Stop and every fail-safe are no-ops right now.
autoControlPanel.strippedForSafety: Stopped for safety: {{reason}}. The heater is off. Move a slider or start control again to continue.
autoControlPanel.heaterChangeHint: The heater changes gradually, never faster than 1% per second, and stops at Drop.

alarmRulesEditor.heading: Automation rules (optional)
alarmRulesEditor.intro: Fire a Burner/Air/Drum command and/or show an in-app banner automatically when a milestone is marked, a temperature threshold is crossed, or a set amount of roast time has elapsed — immediately, or after a delay. Saved as part of this configuration, so it travels with "Save this configuration as" below.
alarmRulesEditor.chainsIntoMarking: Chains this rule's trigger into auto-marking {{milestone}} — same as clicking that button yourself, so it still has to happen in the correct order relative to whatever's already been marked, or it's silently skipped.
alarmRulesEditor.editingRuleAbove: Editing rule #{{n}} above -- "Save changes" replaces it in place, or Cancel to leave it unchanged.
alarmRulesEditor.burnerConfirmIntro: This rule sets Burner to {{pct}}% automatically once {{trigger}}
alarmRulesEditor.burnerConfirmTail: — no further confirmation once saved. Only {{action}} this if you're sure.

connectionTestPanel.heading: Test Connection
connectionTestPanel.simulatedNote: This is a built-in simulated device, so passing checks here say nothing about a real machine -- nothing is sent to hardware.
connectionTestPanel.intro: Verifies the connection is actually working, before committing to a roast -- reads every configured channel for a few seconds.
connectionTestPanel.introModbus: Read + write also confirms Air can be controlled, using the most benign possible write: reading its current value back and writing that exact same value again (a no-op).
connectionTestPanel.introAillio: Read + write also confirms Fan can be controlled, using the most benign possible write: reading its current value back and writing that exact same value again (a no-op).
connectionTestPanel.introTc4: Read + write also confirms Heater can be controlled -- TC4 has no write feedback register at all, so instead of a silent round-trip this briefly bumps OT1 and asks you to confirm you actually saw/heard it respond, then sets it back.
connectionTestPanel.noReading: no {{label}} reading available yet -- can't verify a round-trip
connectionTestPanel.writeMismatch: wrote {{before}}{{suffix}} but feedback now reads {{after}}{{suffix}} -- write may not be reaching the device
connectionTestPanel.writeConfirmed: wrote {{label}} back at its current {{before}}{{suffix}} (no-op) -- feedback confirms it took effect
connectionTestPanel.tc4SkippedHint: TC4's OT1/DCFAN outputs are write-only -- there's no feedback register to read back and confirm against, so use the check below to actually watch/listen for Heater responding.
connectionTestPanel.nudgeExplain: This will briefly bump {{label}} {{direction}} by {{amount}}{{suffix}} for about {{seconds}} seconds (you should see/hear the {{mover}} respond), then set it back to exactly what it was. Only do this if that's fine right now.
connectionTestPanel.restoreFailed: {{label}} is still nudged up -- restoring it to {{value}}{{suffix}} failed: {{message}}. Set it back yourself with the {{label}} slider below, or retry.
connectionTestPanel.confirmedGeneric: ✓ confirmed -- the write path genuinely reaches the hardware{{suffix}}.
connectionTestPanel.notJustFeedback: , not just its own feedback register
connectionTestPanel.modbusAirFailed: ✗ The register write succeeded but nothing physically moved. Air and Drum share identical register numbers and confidence (both blog-sourced only, not independently confirmed) -- Drum is a genuine differential test, not just "try something else."
connectionTestPanel.modbusDrumFailed: ✗ Drum didn't respond either -- that's real evidence the shared register scheme (8192/8193) is wrong for this unit, not just something specific to Air/slave 1. Worth checking your VFD's own nameplate/front-panel parameters against those numbers.
connectionTestPanel.aillioFanFailed: ✗ The device acknowledged the write (no USB error) but nothing physically moved. Fan and Drum use the same underlying command mechanism on this device -- Drum is a genuine differential test, not just "try something else."
connectionTestPanel.aillioDrumFailed: ✗ Drum didn't respond either -- worth double-checking this is genuinely the roaster's own Fan/Drum command (see aillio_bridge/r1.py for the confirmed opcodes) rather than a connection/firmware issue specific to this unit.
connectionTestPanel.tc4Failed: ✗ The OT1 write itself succeeded (no serial error) but nothing visibly responded. Since TC4 has no feedback register at all, this either means a real wiring/SSR problem, or the {{pct}}% bump for {{seconds}}s just wasn't enough to notice -- check the board's own OT1 output directly (multimeter/scope on the pin, or the heating element itself) before assuming the write path is broken.
